top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a mechanism, not just a better number: at the magic wavelength the lattice light shifts both clock levels equally, so many neutral atoms are held Doppler- and recoil-free without a trap-induced line shift. Every systematic is understood quantitatively, theory and experiment agree, and uncertainties near 1e-18 are reproduced in several independent laboratories with cross-site comparisons. The citation can be confined to invention and realisation, which separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Katori holds the proposal and first realisation, and Ye showed the scheme survives at 1e-18 and that many-body and density effects can be controlled. I accept the weaker points: no departure from known physics yet, and Ye's share is the least secure. P003 is next as a genuinely new symmetry class with long replication, though its three-name credit omits Bernevig, Hughes and others and the citation is compound. P002 follows as a clean and consequential measurement, but with credit that is hard to assign within large collaborations and a field where I defer to colleagues. A flawed award still ranks above no award.
recusal_note: Long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with the Lund and Ursula Keller attosecond groups, but none of the proposed laureates (Katori, Ye, Luk, Kim, Wang, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a named collaborator in the profile. No specific conflict apparent from profile, although as an atomic theorist I may have professional familiarity with the lattice-clock field.
